capabilities.verb: Turn any PDF, scan or photo into practice that grades itself
capabilities.summary: Upload course material and the pipeline OCRs scans into searchable markdown, then builds quizzes, exercises and flashcards grounded in your own files.
proofs: Scanned pages OCR into searchable markdown with LaTeX math
Quizzes, exercises and flashcards are generated from your own material
Whiteboard photos get contrast, skew and border preprocessing before OCR
Typed math answers grade through a deterministic equivalence chain (2x = x*2)
Hint-ladder levels 1-4 are code-proven not to reveal the answer; level 5 shows the worked solution

capabilities.verb: Chat with a tutor that has read your course
capabilities.summary: Ask about any node and get answers grounded in your materials with numbered citations; the tutor calls SymPy mid-answer and shows every tool call.
proofs: Answers cite your own materials with numbered sources
A sandboxed calculator and SymPy (solve, diff, integrate) run mid-answer
Mid-answer tools search your library and read your mistakes and due cards
Note edits and study actions apply only through proposal cards you approve

capabilities.verb: Keep your studying on your own machine
capabilities.summary: One local process with a loopback-bound API and keys sealed in the OS keyring; desktop needs no account, self-hosted web adds a login gate.
proofs: The API binds 127.0.0.1 by default; exposure is an explicit choice
API keys live in the OS keyring, never in files, env or the database
Runs fully offline with Ollama, LM Studio or any llama.cpp engine
Scheduled full-archive backups with integrity checks and auto-recovery

capabilities.verb: Remember more with review scheduled for you
capabilities.summary: Flashcards follow an FSRS schedule; due counts surface in the course tree and one global review queue batches everything due today.
proofs: FSRS schedules every card; due counts show per course and node
A keyboard-first review queue runs the whole library, not one deck
Exports to Anki (.apkg) and prints review sheets

capabilities.verb: Capture notes, handwriting and speech that stay searchable
capabilities.summary: Markdown notes with KaTeX and mermaid plus an infinite handwriting canvas join one library; hybrid keyword and semantic search indexes every note, transcript and drawing.
proofs: An infinite handwriting canvas saves crops and its OCR joins the search index
Search fuses FTS5 keyword and vector results, with a typo-tolerant fuzzy tier
Dictate at the cursor; your provider's speech-to-text transcribes into editors and chat
Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K quick capture files a markdown thought from anywhere
A command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K) jumps anywhere and runs full-text search

capabilities.verb: Plan your studying around exams and focus time
capabilities.summary: Import a course timetable from .ics, export any course plan back to calendar files, and track study time with goals, streaks, a focus timer and exam countdowns.
proofs: .ics timetables import as planner items with an explicit exam-date confirmation
Every course plan exports as plan.ics with stable event IDs
A focus timer offers 25/5 and 50/10 presets with a break flow
Daily goals count minutes or answers; streaks and a 90-day heatmap track them
Attempts honor server-enforced time limits with auto-submit

capabilities.verb: Pull material in from the web, your cloud and your reference manager
capabilities.summary: Discover papers on arXiv, OpenAlex and Crossref, connect WebDAV, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Zotero and Anki; every import lands as a suggestion you review.
proofs: arXiv, OpenAlex and Crossref discovery needs no API key
.bib and .ris imports dedupe by DOI; selections export back to BibTeX
OAuth sources use a loopback PKCE flow; tokens are sealed in the OS keyring
Anki reviews merge into the due queue and recompute FSRS deterministically
A WebDAV (or Dropbox) source doubles as a remote backup destination

capabilities.verb: See exactly where your understanding breaks
capabilities.summary: A weakness matrix links concepts to skills, item analysis flags weak questions, and tagged mistakes feed an error-pattern drill generator.
proofs: Weakness matrix maps concepts × skills with coverage per node
Item analysis reports discrimination and distractor efficiency
Tagged mistakes grow error-pattern drills from your own record
Daily, concept and item analytics export to CSV or JSON

capabilities.verb: Extend the app with your own connectors
capabilities.summary: Author source connectors against a versioned manifest contract; external code runs out-of-process and lands only as suggestions you review.
proofs: One validated manifest envelope gates what a connector may do
External connector code runs in its own process (T3), never in-app
A built-in read-only MCP server exposes courses to external AI agents

useCases: Turn a photographed lecture into a graded quiz — snap the whiteboard, OCR it to searchable markdown, generate a quiz with deterministic math grading.
Prepare for an exam from a timetable — import the .ics syllabus, work the global due-queue, then sit a time-limited mock quiz with auto-submit.
Collect thesis sources without leaving the app — discover preprints on arXiv, import .bib with DOI dedupe, connect Zotero, cite from notes.
Study fully offline — point the app at Ollama or LM Studio; OCR, chat, search and dictation run keyless on the machine, nothing leaves it.
Fix recurring mistakes before the retake — the mistake notebook feeds error-pattern drills, and item analysis says what to re-study.
